problem.text: Let $f$ be a function for which $f\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right) = x^2 + x + 1$. Find the sum of all values of $z$ for which $f(3z) = 7$.

steps.title: Where to start: match the input of $f$
steps.body: The formula tells us what $f$ does only when its input is written as $\frac{x}{3}$. We want $f(3z)$, so we need to choose $x$ so that $\frac{x}{3}$ equals $3z$. Careful: putting $x = 3z$ into the formula gives $f(z)$, not $f(3z)$.

steps.title: Write $f(3z)$ as a polynomial in $z$
steps.body:
Replace every $x$ on the right side by $9z$:
$$f(3z) = (9z)^2 + 9z + 1 = 81z^2 + 9z + 1$$

your_turn.prompt: Check the formula with $z = \frac{1}{3}$: it should give $f(1)$. Compare with the original rule using $x = 3$.
your_turn.answer: $81\cdot\frac{1}{9} + 3 + 1 = 13$, and the original rule with $x = 3$ gives $9 + 3 + 1 = 13$. They agree.

steps.title: Set it equal to $7$
steps.body:
Now $f(3z) = 7$ becomes $81z^2 + 9z + 1 = 7$, that is
$$81z^2 + 9z - 6 = 0$$
The values of $z$ we want are the two roots of this quadratic. Before adding them with a shortcut, make sure there really are two real roots.

your_turn.prompt: Compute the discriminant $b^2 - 4ac$ of $81z^2 + 9z - 6$. Is it positive?
your_turn.answer: $81 + 4\cdot 81\cdot 6 = 81\cdot 25 = 2025$, which is positive, so there are two different real roots.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: Vieta's formulas say that the roots of $Az^2 + Bz + C = 0$ add up to $-\frac{B}{A}$. Here that is $-\frac{9}{81} = -\frac{1}{9}$. The answer is **(B)**.

wrong_choices.A: This comes from plugging $x = 3z$ into the formula. That gives $f(z) = 9z^2 + 3z + 1 = 7$, whose roots add to $-\frac{3}{9} = -\frac{1}{3}$, but that equation is about $f(z)$, not $f(3z)$.
